summary: 高欢第六子，废侄高殷自立；留心政事、明察俭约，欲革文宣之弊；皇建二年亲征库莫奚，坠马伤重而崩，传位弟湛。
summary_en: Sixth son of Gao Huan, he deposed his nephew Yin to take the throne; attentive to government, clear-sighted and frugal, he meant to repair Wenxuan's evils; in the 2nd year of Huangjian, campaigning in person against the Kumo Xi, he fell from his horse, his hurt mortal, and died, passing the throne to his brother Zhan.

bio_md:
# 孝昭帝 · 主要事迹

高演字延安，高欢第六子。皇建元年，演与弟湛等废侄高殷，自立为帝，改元皇建。孝昭帝「留心政事」，史称「明察俭约」：即位后大赦改元、任用旧臣，欲革文宣末年之弊；又减轻赋役、整顿吏治，北齐政治为之一新。

然孝昭在位仅一年：皇建二年，亲征库莫奚，堕马伤肋，「遂不能兴」，寻崩，年二十七。临终传位弟高湛（武成帝），以「太子年幼」为由，兄终弟及。史载孝昭临终之悔：因杀废帝高殷，「自以不义」，尝自愧曰「吾尝害济南王」——杀侄夺位之事，终成其心疾。

史评孝昭：「明察俭约，欲革文宣之弊」，然「以篡得位，享年不永」。北齐五帝之中，孝昭最称贤明，惜其短祚；其废侄之事，虽得位不正，然其治绩为北齐短暂之清明。孝昭崩后，武成即位，北齐复入昏暴之途。

> 参考：点校本《北齐书》卷006《孝昭纪》。

bio_parts_en.value:
Gao Yan, styled Yan'an, was the sixth son of Gao Huan. In the 1st year of Huangjian, with his brother Zhan, he deposed his nephew Yin and took the throne himself, changing the era to Huangjian. Xiaozhao "attended to government," the histories calling him "clear-sighted and frugal": on accession he granted amnesty, employed the old ministers, and set out to repair the evils of Wenxuan's last years; he lightened the levies and disciplined the officials, and the government of Qi was renewed for a moment.

But he reigned barely a year: in the 2nd year of Huangjian, campaigning in person against the Kumo Xi, he fell from his horse, hurt his ribs, "and could not rise," dying soon after at twenty-seven. On his deathbed he passed the throne to his brother Zhan (Emperor Wucheng), "the heir being young" — brother succeeding brother. The records tell of his dying remorse: having slain the deposed emperor Yin, "he thought himself unjust," and said, "I once harmed the Prince of Jinan" — the usurpation had become his sickness.

The histories say: "clear-sighted and frugal, he meant to repair Wenxuan's evils," yet "won the throne by usurpation, and his years were few." Of Qi's five sovereigns Xiaozhao was the worthiest — pity his reign was brief; his seizure of the throne was ill-gotten, but his government was the one brief clarity of Qi. With his death Wucheng took the throne, and Qi returned to the dark road.

> References: the punctuated critical edition of the *Bei Qishu*, ch. 6 ("Benji of Emperor Xiaozhao").
